request.text: Welcome to Living Town. This is an architectural inspection of the actual exported assets running in Godot. The extension adds eighty one furnished buildings across five connected districts. The original coastal town and natural reserve remain part of the setting. Slow camera movements reveal the new territory as a connected place, with irregular streets, planted courts, and buildings that respond to their terrain.

The northern harbor quarter adds ten buildings on the landward side of the coast. Its streets bend between small households, shops, workshops, and cafes. Frontages turn toward their own access streets, while side gaps and rear courts keep the blocks from becoming a rigid grid. Notice how the different roof heights and narrow passages give the settlement a more gradual, believable edge.

The western market quarter contains seventeen new buildings. A bent market street and smaller workyard lane organize the neighborhood. Shop rooms, repair spaces, dwellings, and planted courts form a mixed setting rather than isolated repeated boxes. The emphasis is on useful relationships: a clear entrance from the street, service space behind the public rooms, and furniture arranged around the activities inside each building.

Here the hillside district adds twenty three buildings along contour streets. The terrain stays uneven beyond the graded road and foundation pads. Stone plinths support the houses where the slope falls away, and the street follows a controlled elevation profile. These are authored fictional earthworks rather than a surveyed site, but their heights are shared by the planning data, the visible ground, and the generated building foundations.

The orchard edge includes eighteen new buildings around a quieter lane. Garden houses, small shops, and working buildings create a transition between the denser town and the surrounding reserve. Rear planting, flower pots, and occasional trees break up the building fronts. The district is intended to suggest horticultural life and seasonal variation, while keeping entrances, street corridors, and the underlying terrain legible in the exported geometry.

The forest trailhead village adds thirteen buildings beside the retained reserve. Cottages, service rooms, shops, and cycling cafes give this edge a different rhythm from the harbor. Conflicting original vegetation and surface obstacles are cleared around the new development, while the larger woodland remains. One separately generated Infinigen plant prototype is reused in selected courtyards; this is a bounded upstream asset contribution, not an upstream whole town generation run.

At street level, pale plaster, slate, stone, oak, and painted joinery establish the material language. The plaster uses source bound, permissively licensed scanned color, roughness, and normal maps, with restrained weathering baked into a portable color texture. Real window apertures, roof courses, gutters, chimneys, and door surrounds add readable scale. The same conventional material channels travel in the exported glTF assets, rather than depending on Blender procedural shaders.

The extension contains one hundred and fifty three furnished floors and nine hundred and twenty nine room zones. Public rooms, preparation spaces, private rooms, stairs, and landings serve different uses. Compact cafes retain required tables and service counters, with an open stair lobby where needed. Furniture backs, usable fronts, privacy, and pedestrian routes are checked before export; selected focus pieces receive detailed bespoke geometry.

The final view returns to terrain, buildings, and woodland. Roads and pads share one height authority, while the coast and reserve remain. The package includes portable glTF chunks, packed Blender source, semantic identifiers, and collision planning metadata. This Godot capture checks imported visuals and camera presentation. It does not establish playable navigation, physics integration, accessibility, or real time performance; those remain separate consumer tasks.
